title: Australian Salary Calculator: Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Pay (2026–27)
description: Use our australian salary calculator to convert hourly rate to annual salary. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and fortnightly pay. Based on 38-hour week and Fair Work rates.
salarySummary: This australian salary calculator converts your hourly rate to annual gross pay by multiplying by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, then estimates tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (typically 38) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes, you can add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. The calculator then uses that loaded rate for annual and fortnightly estimates.
Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## How the Australian Salary Calculator Works

Our **australian salary calculator** helps you turn an hourly rate into an annual figure, a fortnightly amount, and an estimate of tax and super. The core formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full‑time employees we assume a standard 38‑hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator.

### The Basic Calculation

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For instance, a $30 per hour rate gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 before tax and super. The calculator also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) so you can compare with your payslip.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026 the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the floor set by the Fair Work Commission. Many employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that pays more. The calculator does not assume a specific award; it works from the hourly rate you enter. If you are on an award, check the [pay guides](/blog) for your classification.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. In the calculator you can tick a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator applies it automatically. For example, the minimum casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave.

## Estimating Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross pay, the calculator applies the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax‑free threshold is $18,200, so the first $18,200 you earn is tax‑free. Above that, the rates are:

- 15% for income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% for income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% for income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% for income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. If you are eligible for a reduction or exemption, your actual Medicare may differ. The calculator does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice arrangements.

### Example Tax Calculation

For a gross annual salary of $80,000:
- Tax‑free: $18,200 → $0 tax
- 15% bracket: $45,000 – $18,200 = $26,800 → $4,020 tax
- 30% bracket: $80,000 – $45,000 = $35,000 → $10,500 tax
- Total tax: $14,520
- Medicare levy (2% of $80,000): $1,600
- Total deductions: $16,120
- Net annual pay: $63,880

The calculator shows these steps so you can see how your take‑home pay is derived.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer **on top** of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. The calculator estimates super at 12% of your annual ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on $80,000 gross, the super contribution would be $9,600. This amount goes into your super fund, not your bank account. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. The calculator divides your annual gross by 26 to give a fortnightly figure. For $80,000 gross, that is about $3,076.92 per fortnight before tax. After tax and Medicare, the net fortnightly amount is roughly $2,456.92. You can use this to check your payslip or budget.

## Important Notes and Limitations

This calculator is an estimate. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award‑specific rates, check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. For industry averages, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That is an average, not a median for any particular job. Your own rate may be higher or lower.

## Using the Calculator

To get started, enter your base hourly rate on [the timesheet](/). If you are a casual, tick the casual loading checkbox – the calculator will add 25% on top. Then review your annual, fortnightly, and monthly figures, along with the tax and super estimates. You can also compare different rates or hours to see how changes affect your pay.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38‑hour week is the standard full‑time week under the Fair Work Act. Many awards and agreements use it. If you work part‑time or different hours, simply enter your actual weekly hours in the calculator. The formula remains the same: hourly × hours per week × 52.

## Summary

Our **australian salary calculator** gives you a clear picture of your annual pay, tax, Medicare, and super. It uses the latest Fair Work and ATO figures. Remember that your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, or salary packaging. Use the calculator as a starting point, and always check your payslip and consult a tax professional for personalised advice.
